Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR PACKING OF RAYON STAPLE FIBRES
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 8 December 1966, after the draft finalized by the Man-Made Fibre and Fabric Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been formulated to bring about uniformity in packing of staple fibres in bales. It is hoped that with the adoption of the requirements of packing prescribed in this standard, the staple fibre bales would be able to withstand the normal hazards of transit and reach the destination in a sound condition.

1. SCGPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of packing viscose and acetate rayon staple fibres in the form of bales. 2. PACKING `MATERIALS

2.1 The packing materials conforming to the requirements given in Table 1 shall be used in making up the staple fibre bales. 3. REQUIREMENTS OF BALE PACKING

3.1 The staple fibre bales shall satisfy the following requirements: a) The inner layer of packing shall consist of waxed kraft paper or polyethylene film and the outer layer shall consist of medium weight hessian. The sizes of paper pieces, polyethylene film and cloth shall be such that they are adequate for covering all the sides of the bale when the bale is fully pressed. b) The lips of the end wrapping pieces of medium weight hessian shall be stitched with two strands of 3-ply jute twine of adequate strength. The number of stitches shall be at least 5 per 20 cm. 3

The bales shall be bound with 6 or 7 wire loops uniformly distributed [ see Sl No. (iii) of Table 1 1. The loops shall, be so made that they are in tight condition when the bales are released from the If 6 wire loops are used for binding the bale, then 4 wire If Eig shall be used along the width and 2 along the length, 7 wire loops are used, then all of them may be used for binding along the width. The distance between two successive loops or the distance between the edge and the first loop shall not be more than 22 cm.

d) No wire loop binding the bales shall open up or break when the bales are dropped from a height of 2 m. e) The bales shall be pressed to a density of not more than 500 kg/m*. f) The gross weight of bales shall be at least 150 kg, when fully packed. 4. MARKING

4.1 Bales containing the following:
a) Bale No.,

rayon staple fibres shall be marked on two sides with

b) Gross weight, c) Net weight, 4

d) Fibre denier and whether bright or dull, e) Staple length of fibre, and f) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 4.2 All markings shall be stencilled, writing with hand being not permissible. 4.3 Letters and figures shall be not less than 2.5 cm in height.
